idiom_name: AutoCloseable facade over NIO + kotlinx-io for multiplatform
implementation_notes: On the JVM the facade exists already: java.io/java.nio (Files, Path, channels) wrap the operating system, and Kotlin adds ergonomics rather than structure - kotlin.io extension functions, use { } for scope-based teardown, default arguments and data/sealed classes for the values above the wrapper. kotlinx-io (Buffer/Source/Sink and the FileSystem/Path API) is the multiplatform equivalent when the same code must also build for Kotlin/Native or Wasm, so a hand-written facade is justified only for a third-party C library.
pitfalls: A single NIO operation is atomic but a multi-call protocol is not: header-plus-payload writes still need synchronization inside the facade.
Relying on GC or Cleaner for a native handle is wrong on the JVM - the descriptor stays open until an unpredictable collection, so close explicitly.
Kotlin/Native cinterop declarations are @ExperimentalForeignApi and platform-specific, so they cannot live in the common source set; keep them behind a common interface.

variants.name: Kotlin/Native cinterop binding
variants.idiom_name: cinterop-generated stubs wrapped in a Kotlin class with close()
variants.implementation_notes: For a Kotlin/Native target the cinterop tool reads the C headers and generates the bindings mechanically (types, pointers, structs, enums), so the facade is a Kotlin class holding the generated handle type, translating errors and exposing one close() path. This is the only Kotlin form in which the C API is called without the JVM in between; the generated declarations are @ExperimentalForeignApi, so they stay inside the wrapper and never leak into the public API.
pitfalls: CPointer values are unmanaged: the wrapper must pair every acquire with exactly one release and must not let the pointer escape.
C strings created with cstr inside a call are freed after it returns - storing the resulting pointer keeps a dangling reference.
cinterop output is experimental and per target: it has to be regenerated and re-tested for each platform the project ships.
